Over the past two decades, chikungunya — a viral disease that causes fever and joint pain — has also emerged in more than 100 countries, causing outbreaks in China, Italy and France in the past two years. Last year in Cuba, an outbreak that started in July killed 46 people. Every year, about 14.4 million people worldwide are thought to develop chikungunya, with most of the cases occurring in South Asia and Latin America1. Disease-carrying mosquitoes have now spread to previously unaffected regions in Europe, Asia, the Americas and Australia. Between June 2025 and April 2026, Aedes albopictus — a mosquito that can transmit dengue and chikungunya — spread to new area in several European countries, including Portugal, France and Greece. # Zika virus

## Key facts

## Overview

Zika virus is a mosquito-borne virus that was first identified in Uganda in 1947 in a Rhesus macaque monkey, followed by evidence of infection and disease in humans in other African countries in the 1950s.

From the 1960s to the 1980s, sporadic human infections were detected across Africa and Asia. However, since 2007, outbreaks of Zika virus disease have been recorded in Africa, the Americas, Asia and the Pacific. [...] During outbreaks over the last decade, Zika virus infection was found to be associated with increased incidence of Guillain-Barré syndrome. When Zika virus emerged in the Americas, with a large epidemic in Brazil in 2015, an association between Zika virus infection and microcephaly (smaller than normal head size) was first describe.
